  quantized exactly like the reference's.** The vision copy is composited
  over white by PIL, which works on **uint8**, so every composited pixel
  lands on a level. Doing that arithmetic in float instead leaves 97% of the
  pixels half a level away — and the tower turns that into **rel 3.49 on the
  merged rows and rel 11.1 on the prompt embedding**, which is how this port
  first failed. It is now the stage's negative control, firing at 11115x the
  bound. Read together with the float64 measurement above, the tower
  amplifies an input perturbation by roughly **10³**, and the consequence is

  reproduce the oracle**, so the bicubic resize the endpoint needs has to

  `resize_dst`, 500x333 → 320x224) so it can be gated without staging a
  pipeline. None of this means an edit is fragile — a differently-quantized

On 2026-09-20 the user decided to replace Z-Image-Turbo with
`Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` (cloned at `models/Qwen-Image-2.1/`) for the whole
image vertical — generation *and* edits — accepting that the vertical breaks
during the rework. The plan and live state are in root `IMAGE.md` (stages
Q0–Q9, decisions, open questions); the merged diffusers implementation is
copied verbatim into `reference/qwenimage21/` as the porting oracle. By the
end of 2026-09-20 **Q0–Q7 were done and t2i is served**: `cmd/serve -image`
answers `/v1/images/generations` from a 31.7 GB resident `qimage/pipeline`
(text encoder + DiT + VAE decoder) at **1m38s for 1024²/40 steps**, matching
the fp32 oracle's own picture at mean 3.4e-4, with `background:
"transparent"` returning real alpha and `stream: true` sending in-progress
frames. **The preview decoder is a fitted 64x4 matrix** (`cmd/previewfit`
generates its own training pairs by running the pipeline over 24 prompts) —
159 µs a frame, three partials for 0.3% of a request, so previews have **no
flag**: `-preview`/`-previews` were deleted, not repurposed. **One
capability is still refused naming its stage**: `/v1/images/edits` (Q8 — 2.1
edits by conditional generation, not SDEdit). **Q8 is underway**: the
reference dump (`reference/dump_qi21_vision.py` → `out/qi21vision`, one- and
two-image cases), the 27-layer vision tower on CPU (`qimage/vision`, rel
≤1.1e-4) and the edit text encoding (`qimage/textenc/edit.go` — multi-image
template, 3-D mrope, deepstack injection; `prompt_embeds` 4.3e-4 with one
condition image, 4.8e-4 with two) are done; the pipeline, the
condition-image resize, the GPU ports and the endpoint are not.

**Why:** unified t2i + native multi-reference editing (up to 10 refs), native
RGBA, and a prefix-KV-cache architecture — a capability jump over Z-Image's
SDEdit-based edits, at the cost of 40 undistilled steps (~5x slower per image
until a turbo variant appears).

**How to apply:** read `IMAGE.md` before touching the image vertical; don't
resurrect z-image code paths. `zimage/dit`, `zimage/pipeline`, `cmd/zimage`,
`cmd/ditstack`, `cmd/ditbench` and `cmd/ditblock` were deleted at Q6;
**`zimage/vae` deliberately stayed** because `gpu_conv.go`'s matrix-core
convolution plus `TestGPUConvMatchesScalar` is the validated test bed Q9
wants — it goes once Q9 has taken the packing helpers across. `zimage/qwen`
and `zimage/tokenizer` survive permanently (shared by embed/llm/parakeet);
new model code goes in a `qimage/` tree. `models/Z-Image-Turbo` and
`models/taef1` (62 GB) are unreferenced but still on disk, left for the user

uses gelu_pytorch_tanh while both patch mergers use the exact erf nn.GELU();
the rotation is NeoX halves, *not* qimage/dit's adjacent-pair convention;

while the three deepstack mergers normalize the 4608-wide concatenation
after (the checkpoint's norm widths refuse the swap at load).

content.text:
**Q8.3 — the CPU edit pipeline — is done and gated end to end.**

## What shipped

**The oracle**: `reference/dump_qi21_edit.py` → `out/qi21edit`, deliberately the t2i dump's twin (same size, steps, seed, noise passed in packed). `output_resolution` is set to the card's own size so the pipeline's condition resize is the *identity* — that keeps the gate about the pipeline rather than a resampler. Two runs byte-identical across all 14 tensors.

**Three new pieces**, all small because an edit reuses the t2i graph:
- `dit.LayoutFromPadMask` turns the text encoder's own pad mask into the joint sequence's geometry. It *generalises* `NewLayout` rather than sitting beside it — a t2i prompt has no slots and the two agree, which the test asserts so the edit path can't become a second layout implementation.
- `EncodeCondition` — VAE encode, posterior mode, per-channel normalise, pack.
- `CalcDimensions` — diffusers' geometry, with Python's break-to-even rounding rather than away-from-zero.

## The gate

`TestEndToEndEdit`: condition image + prompt through our own tokenizer, tower, text encoder, VAE encoder, DiT, scheduler and decoder, only the noise from the oracle.

| stage | rel |
|---|---|
| prompt_embeds | 4.7e-4 |
| condition latents | 6.5e-5 |
| per-step latents | 1.4e-4 → 4.4e-5 |
| **edited image** | **max abs 1.0e-5, mean 2e-6** (bound 2.2e-2) |

That's 90x tighter than the t2i gate's own image number — the prefix is why: an edit's trajectory is pinned by 277 rows of conditioning where a generation's is free.

## The finding

The port first missed the oracle's prompt embedding by **rel 11**. The cause wasn't the pipeline: PIL composites alpha over white in **uint8**, so every composited pixel lands on a level, and doing that arithmetic in float leaves 97% of pixels half a level away. The tower turns that into **rel 3.49 on the merged rows**. It's now the stage's negative control, firing at 11115x.

Read with yesterday's float64 measurement, the tower amplifies an input perturbation by roughly **10³** — which is a requirement on work not yet done: an approximate resampler will not reproduce the oracle, so the endpoint's bicubic resize has to match PIL's. The dump carries a before/after pair (500×333 → 320×224) so it can be gated without staging a pipeline. This doesn't make edits fragile — a differently-quantized condition gives a different *valid* edit, as cache-on/off does — but parity is only measurable against the same pixels.

`IMAGE.md`, `TODO.md` and the project memory are updated; `go vet ./...` and the short tests are clean. Not committed — the auto-committer owns `main`. **Still open in Q8:** the bicubic resampler, the GPU ports of the tower and VAE encoder, and the endpoint.

"""Run Qwen-Image-2.1 end to end as an *edit* and dump every step, for Q8.3 —
the oracle the Go edit pipeline is compared against.

`dump_qi21_run.py` is this script's t2i twin and the two are deliberately
alike: same size, same step count, same seed, noise generated here and passed
in packed so the Go side gets it as data. What an edit adds is the prefix —
a condition image that is encoded twice, by the vision tower into text
context and by the VAE into latents the transformer attends over — and this
walks that half:

  * the condition image at both of its resolutions and in both of its copies
    (RGBA for the VAE, flattened over white for the tower);
  * its VAE latents, packed and normalised, which are the `cond` rows the
    denoiser prepends to the target at every step;
  * the prompt embeddings and the image-pad mask the transformer reads the
    layout from;
  * the per-step target latents and the final image.

`output_resolution` is set to the image's own size, which makes the
pipeline's condition resize the identity: that keeps this oracle about the
*pipeline* rather than about a resampler. The resize is a separate question
and is dumped separately at the bottom — `calculate_dimensions` over a
spread of aspect ratios, plus one image the pipeline actually resized, so a
Go resampler can be gated without running any of this.

The whole pipeline in fp32 on CPU is ~68 GB RSS and must run alone.

    .venv/bin/python reference/dump_qi21_edit.py
    .venv/bin/python reference/dump_qi21_edit.py --out reference/out/qi21edit2
"""

import argparse
import json
import os

import numpy as np
import torch
from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline
from PIL import Image

from dump_qi21_vision import test_card

MODEL = "models/Qwen-Image-2.1"
PROMPT = "make the sky a deep orange sunset"
SEED = 42


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="reference/out/qi21edit")
    ap.add_argument("--size", type=int, default=256)
    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=4)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    size, steps = args.size, args.steps
    os.makedirs(args.out, exist_ok=True)

    pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline.from_pretrained(MODEL, torch_dtype=torch.float32)

    manifest = {
        "prompt": PROMPT, "seed": SEED, "size": size, "steps": steps,
        "output_resolution": size, "use_kv_cache": True, "tensors": {},
    }

    def dump(name, t):
        t = t.detach().contiguous().to(torch.float32)
        with open(os.path.join(args.out, name + ".bin"), "wb") as fh:
            fh.write(t.numpy().tobytes())
        flat = t.flatten()
        manifest["tensors"][name] = {
            "shape": list(t.shape), "count": int(flat.numel()),
            "sum": float(flat.double().sum()), "absmax": float(flat.abs().max()),
        }
        print(f"  {name:22s} {str(list(t.shape)):22s} sum={flat.double().sum():+.6f} absmax={flat.abs().max():.5g}")

    # --- the condition image, the same card the tower dump uses ----------
    card = test_card(size)
    rgba = Image.fromarray(card, mode="RGBA")
    dump("cond_rgba", torch.from_numpy(card).permute(2, 0, 1).float()[None] / 127.5 - 1)

    # What the pipeline does to it before either encoder sees it. With
    # output_resolution == the card's own size this is the identity, and the
    # dumped tensor is what proves that rather than an assumption.
    from diffusers.pipelines.qwenimage21.pipeline_qwenimage21 import (  # noqa: PLC0415
        calculate_dimensions,
    )
    in_w, in_h, _ = calculate_dimensions(size * size, card.shape[1] / card.shape[0])
    manifest["cond_input_size"] = [in_w, in_h]
    vae_image = pipe.image_processor.preprocess(rgba, width=in_w, height=in_h).unsqueeze(2)
    dump("cond_vae_image", vae_image)

    # The condition latents: posterior *mode*, per-channel normalised, packed
    # to one row per latent token. These are the rows the denoiser prepends to
    # the target at every step.
    cond_latents = pipe._encode_vae_image(vae_image.to(torch.float32), None)
    dump("cond_latents_grid", cond_latents)
    lat_h, lat_w = cond_latents.shape[3:]
    dump("cond_latents", pipe._pack_latents(cond_latents, 1, 64, lat_h, lat_w))
    manifest["cond_latent_shape"] = [1, int(lat_h), int(lat_w)]

    # --- the prompt side, so a failure can be localised before the loop --
    with torch.no_grad():
        embeds, _, pad_mask = pipe._get_qwen_prompt_embeds(PROMPT, [rgba], device="cpu")
    dump("prompt_embeds", embeds)
    dump("image_pad_mask", pad_mask.float())
    manifest["prompt_tokens"] = int(embeds.shape[1])
    manifest["pad_mask_count"] = int(pad_mask.sum())

    # --- the run ---------------------------------------------------------
    latent_side = size // 16
    generator = torch.Generator("cpu").manual_seed(SEED)
    noise = torch.randn((1, 1, 64, latent_side, latent_side), generator=generator, dtype=torch.float32)
    packed = pipe._pack_latents(noise, 1, 64, latent_side, latent_side)
    dump("noise", packed)

    manifest["img_shapes"] = [[1, int(lat_h), int(lat_w)], [1, latent_side, latent_side]]

    def cb(p, i, t, kw):
        dump(f"step{i}_latents", kw["latents"])
        return kw

    out = pipe(
        prompt=PROMPT,
        image=[rgba],
        width=size, height=size,
        output_resolution=size,
        num_inference_steps=steps,
        latents=packed,
        output_type="np",
        use_kv_cache=True,
        callback_on_step_end=cb,
        callback_on_step_end_tensor_inputs=["latents"],
    )

    image = out.images[0]
    dump("image", torch.from_numpy(image))
    mode = "RGBA" if image.shape[-1] == 4 else "RGB"
    Image.fromarray((image * 255).round().astype(np.uint8), mode).save(os.path.join(args.out, "image.png"))
    manifest["image_mode"] = mode

    # --- the resize, as its own question ---------------------------------
    #
    # Every condition image the server is handed goes through this and almost
    # none of them will be identity like the one above. The geometry is pure
    # arithmetic and is dumped as cases; the resampler is PIL's bicubic and is
    # dumped as one before/after pair, so a Go port can be gated on both
    # without staging a pipeline.
    cases = []
    for res in (256, 1024):
        for w, h in ((256, 256), (192, 384), (384, 192), (500, 333), (1000, 1000)):
            cw, ch, _ = calculate_dimensions(res * res, w / h)
            cases.append({"resolution": res, "src": [w, h], "out": [cw, ch]})
    manifest["calculate_dimensions"] = cases
    wide = Image.fromarray(test_card(size), mode="RGBA").resize((500, 333), Image.BICUBIC)
    dump("resize_src", torch.from_numpy(np.array(wide)).permute(2, 0, 1).float()[None] / 127.5 - 1)
    rw, rh, _ = calculate_dimensions(size * size, 500 / 333)
    manifest["resize_out_size"] = [rw, rh]
    resized = pipe.image_processor.resize(wide, width=rw, height=rh)
    dump("resize_dst", torch.from_numpy(np.array(resized)).permute(2, 0, 1).float()[None] / 127.5 - 1)

    with open(os.path.join(args.out, "manifest.json"), "w") as fh:
        json.dump(manifest, fh, indent=2)
    print(f"wrote {len(manifest['tensors'])} tensors to {args.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

input.new_string:
a requirement on the resampler, which is why it is ported exactly rather
  than approximately (below). None of this means an edit is fragile — a
  differently-quantized condition gives a different *valid* edit, the same
  way cache-on and cache-off do — but it does mean parity is only measurable
  against the same pixels.

  **Q8.3b — the resampler. Done 2026-09-20** (`qimage/pipeline/resize.go`,
  ~200 lines). It is **Lanczos, not bicubic**: `VaeImageProcessor`'s default
  `resample` is `lanczos` and the pipeline constructs it without overriding
  that, so every condition image is resized by
  `PIL.Image.resize(resample=LANCZOS)`. The port reproduces Pillow's
  arithmetic rather than its intent — 22-bit fixed-point coefficients with
  its away-from-zero rounding, an int32 accumulator with its rounding term,
  its clip-and-shift, two passes with a **uint8 intermediate**, and its skip
  of a pass whose axis does not change — and the gate is **exact 8-bit
  equality**, not a tolerance, because at 10³ amplification "close" is not a
  claim worth making.
  Two things had to be got right that reading the filter would not tell you.
  The filter is stretched by the **downscale** factor only, so downscaling
  antialiases and upscaling does not; and **an RGBA image is not resampled
  as four independent channels** — `Image.resize` converts it to `RGBa`
  (premultiplied), resamples, and converts back, both conversions 8-bit and
  lossy. Missing the premultiply left 28% of samples up to four levels out,
  which is how the port first failed. It now matches on all three
  behaviours: **500x333 → 320x224 (down), 128x96 → 288x224 (up), and
  320x224 → 320x112 (one axis)**, every sample of all three exact.

  **Still open in Q8**: the GPU ports of the tower and the VAE encoder, and
  the endpoint.

**The condition resampler is done and bit-exact.**

## The correction up front

I said "bicubic" in my last message. It isn't — `VaeImageProcessor`'s default `resample` is **`lanczos`**, and the pipeline constructs it without overriding that. So every condition image goes through `PIL.Image.resize(resample=LANCZOS)`. I checked the instance rather than trusting the earlier note; docs are corrected.

## What shipped

`qimage/pipeline/resize.go` (~200 lines) reproduces Pillow's *arithmetic*, not its intent: 22-bit fixed-point coefficients with its away-from-zero rounding, an int32 accumulator with its rounding term, its clip-and-shift, two passes with a **uint8 intermediate**, and its skip of a pass whose axis doesn't change. The gate asserts **exact 8-bit equality** rather than a tolerance — at 10³ amplification, "close" isn't a claim worth making.

Two things reading the filter would not have told me:

- **The filter is stretched by the downscale factor only** — downscaling antialiases, upscaling doesn't.
- **An RGBA image is not resampled as four independent channels.** `Image.resize` converts to `RGBa` (premultiplied), resamples, converts back, both conversions 8-bit and lossy. Missing that left 28% of samples up to four levels out — which is exactly how the port first failed, and the gate caught it in one run.

## Gates

| case | result |
|---|---|
| 500×333 → 320×224 (down) | all 286,720 samples exact |
| 128×96 → 288×224 (up) | all 258,048 samples exact |
| 320×224 → 320×112 (one axis) | all 143,360 samples exact |
| identity | unchanged, 666,000 samples |
| `CalcDimensions` | 10 cases exact |

I extended the oracle with the upscale and one-axis pairs deliberately: the first gate only covered downscaling, and a 500×333 photo at `output_resolution` 1024 *upscales* — so the untested branch was the common one. The updated dump is byte-identical across two runs (18 tensors).

`go build`/`go vet ./...` clean, short tests green, docs and memory updated. Not committed — the auto-committer owns `main`.

**Still open in Q8:** the GPU ports of the vision tower and the VAE encoder, then the `/v1/images/edits` endpoint.

Next: the GPU ports. Both block the endpoint (the CPU tower is ~16 min at a 1024² condition), so I'll start with the smaller one — the VAE encoder, which reuses Q5g's decoder graph. Let me see what's there:

421	func (b *builder) wOff(name string) uint32 {
422		off, ok := b.g.weights.off[name]
423		if !ok && b.err == nil && len(b.g.pipes) > 0 {

429	func (b *builder) bOff(name string) uint32 {
430		if off, ok := b.g.weights.off[name]; ok {
431			return off
432		}
433		return noBias
434	}

436	// conv appends a convolution producing a fresh tensor. Both shapes the
437	// decoder uses — 3x3 pad 1 and the 1x1 pad 0 shortcuts and projections —
438	// preserve H and W.
439	func (b *builder) conv(name string, c *zvae.Conv2D, x tensor) tensor {
440		out := tensor{off: b.ar.alloc(c.OutC * x.H * x.W), C: c.OutC, H: x.H, W: x.W}
441		b.label(fmt.Sprintf("conv%dx%d %d->%d @%dx%d", c.KH, c.KW, x.C, c.OutC, x.H, x.W),
442			2*float64(c.OutC)*float64(x.H)*float64(x.W)*float64(x.C)*float64(c.KH)*float64(c.KW))
443		b.pendingIn = x
444		// The grid's y axis is output-channel blocks: the shader holds OC_BLOCK
445		// accumulators per thread, which is where its arithmetic intensity is.
446		const convOCBlock = 8
447		b.addXY("conv2d", groups(out.H*out.W, 256), groups(c.OutC, convOCBlock), pushConstants{
448			InOff: x.off, OutOff: out.off,
449			C: uint32(x.C), H: uint32(x.H), W: uint32(x.W),
450			OC: uint32(c.OutC), KH: uint32(c.KH), KW: uint32(c.KW), Pad: uint32(c.Pad),
451			WOff: b.wOff(name + ".weight"), BOff: b.bOff(name + ".bias"),
452		})
453		return out
454	}

456	// chnorm appends the channel norm, optionally with its SiLU fused. dst may
457	// be src: one thread owns one pixel's whole channel column, so writing it
458	// back over the read is safe and saves a tensor.
459	func (b *builder) chnorm(name string, silu bool, src, dst tensor) tensor {
460		aux := uint32(0)
461		if silu {
462			aux = 1
463		}
464		b.label(fmt.Sprintf("chnorm %d @%dx%d", src.C, src.H, src.W), 0)
465		b.add("chnorm", groups(src.H*src.W, 256), pushConstants{
466			InOff: src.off, OutOff: dst.off,
467			C: uint32(src.C), H: uint32(src.H), W: uint32(src.W),
468			WOff: b.wOff(name + ".gamma"),
469			Aux0: aux,
470		})
471		return dst
472	}
473	
474	// addInto appends a += res.
475	func (b *builder) addInto(a, res tensor) tensor {
476		b.add("add", groups(a.elems(), 256), pushConstants{
477			InOff: a.off, OutOff: a.off, ResOff: res.off, Aux0: uint32(a.elems()),
478		})
479		return a
480	}
481	
482	// resblock records one residual block. keepIn leaves the input allocated,
483	// which the up blocks need: their parameter-free shortcut reads the block's
484	// input after all three resnets have run.
485	//
486	// Every release happens after the dispatch that consumes the tensor is
487	// recorded and after the next tensor is allocated; releasing earlier would
488	// let the allocator hand the same block to a tensor still being read.
489	func (b *builder) resblock(name string, r *ResBlock, x tensor, keepIn bool) tensor {
490		// norm1 writes into a fresh tensor rather than over x: x is the residual
491		// and is read again at the end of the block.
492		h := tensor{off: b.ar.alloc(x.elems()), C: x.C, H: x.H, W: x.W}
493		b.chnorm(name+".norm1", true, x, h)
494	
495		h1 := b.conv(name+".conv1", &r.Conv1, h)
496		b.release(h)
497		b.chnorm(name+".norm2", true, h1, h1)
498	
499		h2 := b.conv(name+".conv2", &r.Conv2, h1)
500		b.release(h1)
501	
502		skip := x
503		if r.Shortcut != nil {
504			skip = b.conv(name+".shortcut", r.Shortcut, x)
505		}
506		out := b.addInto(h2, skip)
507		if r.Shortcut != nil {
508			b.release(skip)
509		}
510		if !keepIn {
511			b.release(x)
512		}
513		return out
514	}
515	
516	// attention records the mid block's single-head spatial attention. The three
517	// projections are the three row blocks of to_qkv's [3C, C] weight, read at
518	// offsets; the output projection is its own 1x1. Both run on vae_linear over
519	// the pixel rows, which is what a 1x1 convolution is once the tensor is
520	// transposed out of NCHW.
521	func (b *builder) attention(name string, a *Attention, x tensor) tensor {
522		rows := x.H * x.W
523		dim := x.C
524	
525		h := tensor{off: b.ar.alloc(x.elems()), C: x.C, H: x.H, W: x.W}
526		b.chnorm(name+".norm", false, x, h)
527	
528		seq := tensor{off: b.ar.alloc(rows * dim), C: dim, H: x.H, W: x.W}
529		b.add("to_rows", groups(rows*dim, 256), pushConstants{
530			InOff: h.off, OutOff: seq.off,
531			C: uint32(dim), H: uint32(x.H), W: uint32(x.W),
532		})
533		b.release(h)
534	
535		qkvW, qkvB := b.wOff(name+".qkv.weight"), b.wOff(name+".qkv.bias")
536		proj := func(which int) tensor {
537			out := tensor{off: b.ar.alloc(rows * dim), C: dim, H: x.H, W: x.W}
538			b.label(fmt.Sprintf("linear %d->%d x%d", dim, dim, rows), 2*float64(rows)*float64(dim)*float64(dim))
539			b.add("linear", groups(rows*dim, 64), pushConstants{
540				InOff: seq.off, OutOff: out.off,
541				C: uint32(dim), H: uint32(x.H), W: uint32(x.W), OC: uint32(dim),
542				WOff: qkvW + uint32(which*dim*dim), BOff: qkvB + uint32(which*dim),
543			})
544			return out
545		}
546		q, k, v := proj(0), proj(1), proj(2)
547		b.release(seq)
548	
549		// Transpose K so the score loop reads consecutive keys at consecutive
550		// addresses. The +64 pads the row stride off a multiple of the 4 KB
551		// channel rotation (IDEAS §5.1b).
552		kStride := rows + 64
553		kT := tensor{off: b.ar.alloc(dim * kStride), C: dim, H: 1, W: kStride}
554		b.label(fmt.Sprintf("transpose %dx%d", rows, dim), 0)
555		b.add("transpose", groups(rows*dim, 256), pushConstants{
556			InOff: k.off, OutOff: kT.off,
557			C: uint32(dim), Aux0: uint32(rows), Aux1: uint32(kStride),
558		})
559		b.release(k)
560	
561		ctx := tensor{off: b.ar.alloc(rows * dim), C: dim, H: x.H, W: x.W}
562		// Two passes of q.k plus the weighted sum of v, all over rows x rows.
563		b.label(fmt.Sprintf("attention %d rows x %d", rows, dim),
564			3*2*float64(rows)*float64(rows)*float64(dim))
565		b.add("attention", uint32(rows), pushConstants{
566			InOff: q.off, OutOff: ctx.off, ResOff: kT.off,
567			C:      uint32(dim),
568			Groups: uint32(kStride),
569			Aux0:   uint32(rows), Aux1: math.Float32bits(float32(1 / math.Sqrt(float64(dim)))), Aux2: v.off,
570		})
571		b.release(q, kT, v)
572	
573		outRows := tensor{off: b.ar.alloc(rows * dim), C: dim, H: x.H, W: x.W}
574		b.label(fmt.Sprintf("linear %d->%d x%d", dim, dim, rows), 2*float64(rows)*float64(dim)*float64(dim))
575		b.add("linear", groups(rows*dim, 64), pushConstants{
576			InOff: ctx.off, OutOff: outRows.off,
577			C: uint32(dim), H: uint32(x.H), W: uint32(x.W), OC: uint32(dim),
578			WOff: b.wOff(name + ".proj.weight"), BOff: b.bOff(name + ".proj.bias"),
579		})
580		b.release(ctx)
581	
582		res := tensor{off: b.ar.alloc(x.elems()), C: x.C, H: x.H, W: x.W}
583		// The bias is already in the projection above, so the fused add has none
584		// of its own — and there is no push-constant value that means "unset", so
585		// it is said explicitly.
586		b.add("to_nchw", groups(x.elems(), 256), pushConstants{
587			InOff: outRows.off, OutOff: res.off, ResOff: x.off,
588			C: uint32(x.C), H: uint32(x.H), W: uint32(x.W),
589			Aux0: noBias,
590		})
591		b.release(outRows, x)
592		return res
593	}

14	// The decoder on the device — IMAGE.md Q5g, the stage that stood between
15	// Q4's 2.27 s DiT step and a served image.
16	//
17	// The CPU decoder in vae.go is the oracle and is also the reason this file
18	// exists: it decodes 256x256 in ~20 s, and the graph is 16x larger at
19	// 1024x1024, so a served generation would have spent minutes downstream of
20	// a 91 s transformer.
21	//
22	// Almost none of it is new. z-image's decoder graph (zimage/vae/gpu.go)
23	// established the shape — one weight arena written once, one activation
24	// arena a bump allocator ping-pongs inside, "which tensor" as an offset
25	// rather than a descriptor rebind, and the whole decode recorded as a
26	// dispatch list — and its kernels do the work here unchanged: the
27	// register-blocked fp32 convolution, the 2x nearest upsample, the add, and
28	// the mid block's row-major attention with its transposed K. Three things
29	// in this VAE are genuinely not in that one, and each is one shader:
30	//
31	//   - the norm. RMS_norm here is a per-pixel L2 normalize across channels,
32	//     not a group norm, and it is always followed by a SiLU — qvae_chnorm
33	//     does both in one pass;
34	//   - the up blocks' parameter-free channel-to-space shortcut, whose
35	//     channel mapping depends on a video model's temporal factor even
36	//     though no temporal axis survives at T = 1 — qvae_dupup;
37	//   - the mid block is 1152 channels wide where z-image's is 512, which the
38	//     scalar attention kernel needs as a compile-time bound.
39	//
40	// The mid block's four projections are 1x1 convolutions, which is to say
41	// linears over the pixel rows, and to_qkv's [3C, C] weight is three of them
42	// stacked — so the graph reads it at three offsets rather than splitting the
43	// tensor. That is why there is no qkv convolution in the dispatch list.
44	//
45	// Everything here is fp32. Q0 measured this decoder's intermediates at
46	// absmax ~1e5–3e5 against fp16's 65504, so the matrix-core convolution that
47	// took z-image's decode from 3.18 s to 258 ms cannot simply be pointed at
48	// this graph; what it would take is priced in gpu_test.go's range

52	// pipeline in the graph declares the same block, because vk.DispatchMultiTimed
53	// records the whole thing into one command buffer and requires one
54	// push-constant size across it.
55	type pushConstants struct {
56		InOff, OutOff    uint32
57		C, H, W          uint32
58		OC, KH, KW, Pad  uint32

67	}

73	// back as VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST; the same dispatches submitted in batches all
74	// complete. 4 is z-image's measured-free value and this graph's dispatches

102	func (a *arena) alloc(elems int) uint32 {
103		n := roundUp(elems)
104		best := -1
105		for i, b := range a.free {
106			if b.size >= n && (best < 0 || b.size < a.free[best].size) {
107				best = i
108			}
109		}
110		if best >= 0 {
111			blk := a.free[best]
112			a.free = append(a.free[:best], a.free[best+1:]...)

  pad computes exactly what the stride-1 pad-1 form computes at the *odd*

  — which keeps (2h+1, 2w+1) — is reused unmodified and the ordinary
  convolution does the work, at four times the arithmetic and no second
  shader. Genuinely new: `qvae_avgdown`, the mirror of `qvae_dupup`, whose
  temporal factor at T = 1 still averages in a **zero frame** and still
  divides by the full group; and a second build of the attention kernel,

  (base_dim 96 against decoder_base_dim 144) and DIM is a shared-array
  extent rather than a push constant.

  weights, arena — the same split `zimage/vae` made between its own two
  directions, so the second graph added no Vulkan lifecycle at all.

On 2026-09-20 the user decided to replace Z-Image-Turbo with
`Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` (cloned at `models/Qwen-Image-2.1/`) for the whole
image vertical — generation *and* edits — accepting that the vertical breaks
during the rework. The plan and live state are in root `IMAGE.md` (stages
Q0–Q9, decisions, open questions); the merged diffusers implementation is
copied verbatim into `reference/qwenimage21/` as the porting oracle. By the
end of 2026-09-20 **Q0–Q7 were done and t2i is served**: `cmd/serve -image`
answers `/v1/images/generations` from a 31.7 GB resident `qimage/pipeline`
(text encoder + DiT + VAE decoder) at **1m38s for 1024²/40 steps**, matching
the fp32 oracle's own picture at mean 3.4e-4, with `background:
"transparent"` returning real alpha and `stream: true` sending in-progress
frames. **The preview decoder is a fitted 64x4 matrix** (`cmd/previewfit`
generates its own training pairs by running the pipeline over 24 prompts) —
159 µs a frame, three partials for 0.3% of a request, so previews have **no
flag**: `-preview`/`-previews` were deleted, not repurposed. **One
capability is still refused naming its stage**: `/v1/images/edits` (Q8 — 2.1
edits by conditional generation, not SDEdit). **Q8 is underway**: the
reference dump (`reference/dump_qi21_vision.py` → `out/qi21vision`, one- and
two-image cases), the 27-layer vision tower on CPU (`qimage/vision`, rel
≤1.1e-4) and the edit text encoding (`qimage/textenc/edit.go` — multi-image
template, 3-D mrope, deepstack injection; `prompt_embeds` 4.3e-4 with one
condition image, 4.8e-4 with two) and the CPU edit pipeline (end to end
against `out/qi21edit`, the edited image at max abs 1.0e-5) and the
condition resampler (Pillow **Lanczos**, not bicubic — bit-exact) are done;
the GPU ports and the endpoint are not.

**Why:** unified t2i + native multi-reference editing (up to 10 refs), native
RGBA, and a prefix-KV-cache architecture — a capability jump over Z-Image's
SDEdit-based edits, at the cost of 40 undistilled steps (~5x slower per image
until a turbo variant appears).

**How to apply:** read `IMAGE.md` before touching the image vertical; don't
resurrect z-image code paths. `zimage/dit`, `zimage/pipeline`, `cmd/zimage`,
`cmd/ditstack`, `cmd/ditbench` and `cmd/ditblock` were deleted at Q6;
**`zimage/vae` deliberately stayed** because `gpu_conv.go`'s matrix-core
convolution plus `TestGPUConvMatchesScalar` is the validated test bed Q9
wants — it goes once Q9 has taken the packing helpers across. `zimage/qwen`
and `zimage/tokenizer` survive permanently (shared by embed/llm/parakeet);
new model code goes in a `qimage/` tree. `models/Z-Image-Turbo` and
`models/taef1` (62 GB) are unreferenced but still on disk, left for the user
to remove. **Three hard numbers to remember**: the VAE decoder's activation
arena is a single storage buffer against this device's 4 GiB−4 cap, so
**1184x1184 is the largest square that decodes** (2048², the model card's
own example size, does not); the **step count is prompt-dependent** —
photographic/painterly prompts hold at 12 steps, structured technical
drawings break below 24, which is why the default stays 40; and a **preview
decodes the denoised estimate x0, never the sample x_t** (2.5x worse at
step 0, asserted as a negative control in TestPreviewFrames).

**Four traps in the vision tower**, each a firing negative control in
`qimage/vision`: token order is 2x2-block-major not raster; the block MLP
uses gelu_pytorch_tanh while both patch mergers use the exact erf nn.GELU();
the rotation is NeoX halves, *not* qimage/dit's adjacent-pair convention;
and the output merger normalizes each 1152-row before concatenating four
while the three deepstack mergers normalize the 4608-wide concatenation
after (the checkpoint's norm widths refuse the swap at load).
The dump env is the shared `.venv`: transformers 5.17.0 is fine (diffusers'
final-norm hook verified there, Q0), diffusers is pinned to git `80c7ed26`
(0.41.0.dev0 — stable 0.40.0 lacks the classes). The fp32 torch text-encoder
probes take ~34 GB and the full-pipeline oracle ~68 GB — **one at a time**:
on 2026-09-20 a 34 GB Go encoder test beside the running oracle got both
OOM-killed (the kernel picked the python at step 8 of 40). taehv's taew2_1 does
NOT fit this model's 64-channel/16x VAE — previews are a self-fitted linear
64→RGB matrix until upstream ships a real tiny decoder. See
[[docs-consolidated-into-research]], [[deployment-two-machines]].

content.text:
**The VAE encoder is on the GPU.** A 1024² condition image encodes in **1.65–1.72 s** over 94 dispatches, against a CPU encoder costing minutes at that size — paid per reference image, per request.

## What shipped

`qimage/vae/gpu_encoder.go` (~300 lines). It's small because the encoder is the decoder's graph read backwards over the same kernels, and the piece that *looked* like new work wasn't:

- **The stride-2 downsampler needs no kernel.** z-image's encoder had already established that a 3×3 stride-2 conv over a (0,1,0,1) pad computes exactly what the stride-1 pad-1 form computes at the **odd** pixels. Qwen's downsampler has the identical shape, so `vae_downsample2x` — which keeps (2h+1, 2w+1) — is reused unmodified.
- **Genuinely new:** `qvae_avgdown` (mirror of `qvae_dupup`; at T=1 its temporal factor still averages in a *zero frame* and still divides by the full group), and a `-DDIM=768` attention build, because the encoder's mid block is 768 wide against the decoder's 1152 and DIM is a shared-array extent.

I also factored the Vulkan lifecycle into a shared `engine` — the same split `zimage/vae` made between its two directions — so the second graph added no boilerplate. I re-ran the decoder's GPU tests first and after: 7.04 s at 1024², unchanged.

## Gates

On `vae_test.go`'s existing bounds, both dump cases, every stage: **conv_in 1.1e-6 → all five down blocks → mid block → fused tail norm → conv_out → posterior mode 2.6e-5**, normalised mode 2.9e-5, and a direct **GPU-vs-CPU encode at 4.6e-5**.

Two controls fire: the symmetric-pad stride-2 downsampler is **refused at construction**, and the AvgDown temporal factor lands at **12173x** the bound. That second one is worth flagging — it first *passed for the wrong reason*. I was breaking the temporal factor on whichever blocks had one but measuring `down_blocks.0`, which has none (`temperal_downsample` is `[false, true, true, true]`). A control that can't see the thing it breaks isn't a control; it now measures the first block that actually has a temporal factor.

Docs and memory updated; `go build`/`go vet ./...` clean; full `qimage/vae` package green (175 s).

**Still open in Q8:** the GPU vision tower — the last blocker — then the `/v1/images/edits` endpoint. Worth noting going in: the tower's residual stream reaches absmax 1.4e4, and Q8.2 measured it amplifying input perturbations by ~10³, so an fp16 port there is the one place in this vertical where precision is a real design question rather than a rounding detail.

func (g *GPU) allocActivations() error {
	alloc := func(n int) uint32 {
		off := uint32(g.actElems)
		g.actElems += (n + 63) &^ 63
		return off
	}
	rows := g.tokPad
	g.aX = alloc(rows * g.dim)
	g.aQ = alloc(rows * g.dim)
	g.aK = alloc(rows * g.dim)
	g.aV = alloc(rows * g.dim)
	g.aCtx = alloc(rows * g.dim)
	g.aAttn = alloc(rows * g.dim)
	g.aGate = alloc(rows * g.ffn)
	g.aUp = alloc(rows * g.ffn)
	g.aFF = alloc(rows * g.dim)
	g.aMod = alloc(10 * g.dim)
	g.aLat = alloc(rows * 64)
	g.aOut = alloc(rows * g.outChannels)
	g.aCache = alloc(len(g.blocks) * 2 * g.maxPrefix * g.dim)

	halloc := func(n int) uint32 {
		off := uint32(g.hElems)
		g.hElems += (n + 63) &^ 63
		return off
	}
	plane := g.heads * g.tokPad * g.headDim
	g.hA = halloc(rows * g.ldaDim)
	g.hQ = halloc(plane)
	g.hK = halloc(plane)
	g.hV = halloc(plane)
	g.hCtx = halloc(rows * g.ldaDim)
	g.hFFN = halloc(rows * g.ldaFFN)
	g.hLat = halloc(rows * g.ldaLat)

	var err error
	if g.abuf, err = g.dev.NewBuffer(g.actElems * 4); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("dit: fp32 activation arena (%d MB): %w", (g.actElems*4)>>20, err)
	}
	if g.hbuf, err = g.dev.NewBuffer(g.hElems * 2); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("dit: fp16 activation arena (%d MB): %w", (g.hElems*2)>>20, err)
	}
	// Zero the fp16 arena once: pad rows and columns of every A operand and
	// the attention tail read from here.
	g.hbuf.WriteFloat32(make([]float32, g.hElems/2))
	return nil
}

20	//
21	// **Precision was measured before it was chosen** (TestFP16Ladder). This
22	// tower sits between the two conventions already in the tree: the VAE is
23	// fp32 because its activations reach 1e5 against half's 65504, and the DiT
24	// and text encoder are fp16 on the matrix cores because that is where their
25	// speed is. The tower's residual stream reaches absmax 1.3e4 — inside half's
26	// range but with three decimal digits left — and Q8.2 measured the tower
27	// amplifying perturbations by ~1600x. Running every linear with fp16
28	// operands and fp32 accumulation on the CPU oracle costs **rel 0.14 on the
29	// merged rows** and does not overflow, which is what said the matrix cores
30	// are usable here and what this port is gated against. For scale: the
31	// checkpoint's own bf16 pipeline deviates from fp32 by rel 2.0 on the text
32	// embedding it ultimately feeds.

35	// and three reuses are worth naming because they are not obvious:
36	//
37	//   - **the affine LayerNorm is dit_final_norm plus algebra.** That kernel
38	//     computes LN(x) * scale and narrows to fp16; the ViT wants
39	//     LN(x) * gamma + beta feeding a linear W(.) + b. Since
40	//     W(LN(x)*gamma + beta) + b = W(LN(x)*gamma) + (W*beta + b), the beta is
41	//     folded into the following projection's bias at load time and the
42	//     kernel is used verbatim;
43	//   - **the residual add is dit_gate_add with its gate dropped** (aux2 = 0),
44	//     which is the path the DiT's two unmodulated blocks already take;
45	//   - **the patch merger's concatenation is free.** Four consecutive rows of
46	//     1152 in a row-major buffer *are* one row of 4608, so the output
47	//     merger normalises with a tight row stride and the GEMM reads the same
48	//     bytes four rows at a time, while the three deepstack mergers normalise

**Q8.3d — the vision tower on the GPU. Done 2026-09-20**
  (`qimage/vision/gpu.go`, ~600 lines; `qvit_bias_act.comp` and
  `qvit_rope.comp` are the only new shaders). **A 1024² condition image runs
  the 27 blocks in 6.27 s** — two runs 6.283/6.265 — against roughly twenty
  minutes on the CPU port, and about 6% of an edit's total.
  **The precision was measured before it was chosen**, which is the part
  worth keeping. This tower sits between the tree's two conventions: the VAE
  is fp32 because its activations reach 1e5 against half's 65504, the DiT
  and text encoder are fp16 on the matrix cores because that is where their
  speed is, and this one's residual stream reaches absmax 1.3e4 — inside
  half's range but with three digits left — while Q8.2 measured the tower
  amplifying perturbations by ~1600x. So `TestFP16Ladder` runs the *CPU
  oracle* with every linear taking fp16 operands and accumulating in fp32,
  which is what a matrix core does, and reports **rel 0.135 at the last
  hidden state, 0.14 on the merged rows, no overflow** — sub-linear growth
  from 3.6e-3 at block 0. That is what said the matrix cores are usable, and
  it is the bound the port is gated at. The device then landed **within a
  few percent of the prediction at every stage** (merged 0.127 against 0.14,
  deepstack 0.016/0.031/0.050 against 0.015/0.035/0.053), which is better
  evidence of a correct port than the bound itself: a structural mistake in
  this tower moves these tensors by rel 0.76 to 8.1, per the four controls
  `qimage/vision` already carries.
  Almost every kernel is the DiT's, and three of the reuses are the reason
  the file is small. **The affine LayerNorm is `dit_final_norm` plus
  algebra**: that kernel computes LN(x)·scale, the ViT wants LN(x)·γ + β
  feeding W(·) + b, and W(LN(x)·γ + β) + b = W(LN(x)·γ) + (W·β + b) — so β
  is folded into the next projection's bias at load and the kernel is used
  verbatim. **The residual add is `dit_gate_add` with its gate dropped**,
  the path the DiT's two unmodulated blocks already take. **The patch
  merger's concatenation is free**: four consecutive rows of 1152 in a
  row-major buffer *are* one row of 4608, so the output merger normalises
  with a tight row stride and the GEMM reads the same bytes four rows at a
  time, while the three deepstack mergers normalise the 4608 directly.
  Attention is the **scalar** kernel, which takes its head width from a push
  constant and runs this tower's 72 unchanged; the matrix-core one is built
  per head dim and 72 does not divide its 16-wide tile. Padding to 80 would
  work and is a **percent, not a capability** — the 6.27 s says whether it is
  worth it, and at 6% of an edit it is not yet. The MLP's 4304 is padded to
  4352 for the same tile reason, with zeros that GELU fixes at zero and the
  second layer multiplies by zero rows.

  **Still open in Q8**: the endpoint.

On 2026-09-20 the user decided to replace Z-Image-Turbo with
`Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` (cloned at `models/Qwen-Image-2.1/`) for the whole
image vertical — generation *and* edits — accepting that the vertical breaks
during the rework. The plan and live state are in root `IMAGE.md` (stages
Q0–Q9, decisions, open questions); the merged diffusers implementation is
copied verbatim into `reference/qwenimage21/` as the porting oracle. By the
end of 2026-09-20 **Q0–Q7 were done and t2i is served**: `cmd/serve -image`
answers `/v1/images/generations` from a 31.7 GB resident `qimage/pipeline`
(text encoder + DiT + VAE decoder) at **1m38s for 1024²/40 steps**, matching
the fp32 oracle's own picture at mean 3.4e-4, with `background:
"transparent"` returning real alpha and `stream: true` sending in-progress
frames. **The preview decoder is a fitted 64x4 matrix** (`cmd/previewfit`
generates its own training pairs by running the pipeline over 24 prompts) —
159 µs a frame, three partials for 0.3% of a request, so previews have **no
flag**: `-preview`/`-previews` were deleted, not repurposed. **One
capability is still refused naming its stage**: `/v1/images/edits` (Q8 — 2.1
edits by conditional generation, not SDEdit). **Q8 is underway**: the
reference dump (`reference/dump_qi21_vision.py` → `out/qi21vision`, one- and
two-image cases), the 27-layer vision tower on CPU (`qimage/vision`, rel
≤1.1e-4) and the edit text encoding (`qimage/textenc/edit.go` — multi-image
template, 3-D mrope, deepstack injection; `prompt_embeds` 4.3e-4 with one
condition image, 4.8e-4 with two) and the CPU edit pipeline (end to end
against `out/qi21edit`, the edited image at max abs 1.0e-5) and the
condition resampler (Pillow **Lanczos**, not bicubic — bit-exact) and the
GPU VAE encoder (1024² in 1.7 s) are done; the GPU vision tower and the
endpoint are not.

**Why:** unified t2i + native multi-reference editing (up to 10 refs), native
RGBA, and a prefix-KV-cache architecture — a capability jump over Z-Image's
SDEdit-based edits, at the cost of 40 undistilled steps (~5x slower per image
until a turbo variant appears).

**How to apply:** read `IMAGE.md` before touching the image vertical; don't
resurrect z-image code paths. `zimage/dit`, `zimage/pipeline`, `cmd/zimage`,
`cmd/ditstack`, `cmd/ditbench` and `cmd/ditblock` were deleted at Q6;
**`zimage/vae` deliberately stayed** because `gpu_conv.go`'s matrix-core
convolution plus `TestGPUConvMatchesScalar` is the validated test bed Q9
wants — it goes once Q9 has taken the packing helpers across. `zimage/qwen`
and `zimage/tokenizer` survive permanently (shared by embed/llm/parakeet);
new model code goes in a `qimage/` tree. `models/Z-Image-Turbo` and
`models/taef1` (62 GB) are unreferenced but still on disk, left for the user
to remove. **Three hard numbers to remember**: the VAE decoder's activation
arena is a single storage buffer against this device's 4 GiB−4 cap, so
**1184x1184 is the largest square that decodes** (2048², the model card's
own example size, does not); the **step count is prompt-dependent** —
photographic/painterly prompts hold at 12 steps, structured technical
drawings break below 24, which is why the default stays 40; and a **preview
decodes the denoised estimate x0, never the sample x_t** (2.5x worse at
step 0, asserted as a negative control in TestPreviewFrames).

**Four traps in the vision tower**, each a firing negative control in
`qimage/vision`: token order is 2x2-block-major not raster; the block MLP
uses gelu_pytorch_tanh while both patch mergers use the exact erf nn.GELU();
the rotation is NeoX halves, *not* qimage/dit's adjacent-pair convention;
and the output merger normalizes each 1152-row before concatenating four
while the three deepstack mergers normalize the 4608-wide concatenation
after (the checkpoint's norm widths refuse the swap at load).
The dump env is the shared `.venv`: transformers 5.17.0 is fine (diffusers'
final-norm hook verified there, Q0), diffusers is pinned to git `80c7ed26`
(0.41.0.dev0 — stable 0.40.0 lacks the classes). The fp32 torch text-encoder
probes take ~34 GB and the full-pipeline oracle ~68 GB — **one at a time**:
on 2026-09-20 a 34 GB Go encoder test beside the running oracle got both
OOM-killed (the kernel picked the python at step 8 of 40). taehv's taew2_1 does
NOT fit this model's 64-channel/16x VAE — previews are a self-fitted linear
64→RGB matrix until upstream ships a real tiny decoder. See
[[docs-consolidated-into-research]], [[deployment-two-machines]].
